response.text:
CL4SRec uses random contiguous cropping, item masking and local reordering to create contrastive views; cropping is not inherently supervised suffix prediction. Its relevant control compares ordinary SASRec, augmentation-only SASRec_aug, and augmentation plus contrastive loss. Augmentation alone gives mixed improvements; contrastive learning improves all reported augmentation variants. Sweeping λ in Lmain + λLcontrastive shows that excessive auxiliary weight hurts recommendation. These experiments motivate augmentation-only and loss-weight controls, but do not establish a NextItNet suffix advantage. [CL4SRec paper, §§4.3–4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.14395).

SSS4SR studies prefix, suffix and sliding-window splitting crossed with single-/multi-target supervision and CE/BCE. Its central finding: splitting changes target coverage and frequency, so apparent architectural improvements can reflect additional supervision. Gains generally diminish or reverse with multi-target full-catalog CE, where eligible interactions already receive supervision. Its detailed factorial experiments cover GRU4Rec, SASRec, FMLPRec and BSARec; NextItNet appears in baseline comparisons. It does not establish matched top-k-loss results for NextItNet. [SSS4SR, §§4–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05309v1).

Suggested NextItNet ablation, inferred from these findings: sample identical training targets and compare each target’s full available prefix against a recent suffix ending immediately before that target. Cross input choice with CE alone and CE plus the same precisely defined top-k auxiliary loss. Match target counts, target sampling, negatives, updates and dropout; average losses over valid targets and sweep auxiliary weight including zero. Add a repeated-full-prefix branch with independent dropout and identical weighting to control for extra stochastic supervision. Compare random contiguous contexts with length-matched recent suffixes to test recency specifically. Keep one jointly trained causal model per category, exclude targets from inputs, and read the final nonpadding position.
